十月一日，是祖国母亲的生日，而十月四日，则是我亲爱的妈妈的生日，所以我们决定四日回家给母亲庆祝生日哦。

![20261004_163558.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTPbdQF6pDdbRKPwSgh4KK6FVZpmf5KPnzPZ5sziBDcx6/20261004_163558.jpg)

其实我早早就想回家，然后带母亲来我家里，在我们这边过生日，这样就可以选一些好的饭店吃大餐啦。

可是母亲说姐姐姐夫工作忙，又要给她过生日，来回跑沈阳太麻烦啦，所以坚决留在老家过生日，反正我们十一期间也得回去，那就依她在老家过生日吧。

最近一段时间，我这边事情特别多，孩子作业也不少，所以我们选择四日当天早早出发。

结果到了三号晚上，朋友圈、微信群、公众号都在说四号有大雨、暴雨、大暴雨、冰雹啥的，告诉大家不要出行，呜呜呜，早知道我们三号一早走就好了。

不过后悔也没有用啦，只能等四号早早起床，见机行事啦。

结果四号我睡醒一看，大暴雨已经停歇了，天气转晴，太适合出行啦。于是喊媳妇和儿子赶紧收拾东西，出发。

以往节假日高速公路回家，耗时三四个小时都算是少的啦，结果四号我们回家只耗时一个半小时多一点，莫非是大家都觉得当天有大暴雨，没敢出行的缘故？

一路顺畅地开回老家。

老父亲弄的葡萄架，令人惊奇的是，竟然还有葡萄。
![20261004_105803.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZgUBovmCN4HgJFHm7oxQmzRBMyUD9TuvrSN1cKeBnENu/20261004_105803.jpg)

老父亲说是已经是第二茬葡萄啦，看着不错，但吃起来特别算，和第一茬的口感没法比，哈哈，那也不错啦。
![20261004_105809.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYWq3TKv3MJDnCLQALAtkuSAyUYxeA5NXUSrF98Uuj7Dy/20261004_105809.jpg)

家里有好多棵枣树，枣子特别香甜
![20261004_105823.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVNGgjaHgU18KkACu1VmL3cvLTVuvRs85oxqFU8oaKivo/20261004_105823.jpg)

还有杏树，不过杏早就被吃光啦
![20261004_105838.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmerUYPxA2E2QWwfLXsEPJ3Fvk7FnRk1HvnqFuF9fX8cyc/20261004_105838.jpg)

又是枣树，我想起鲁迅的：我家门口有两棵树，一棵是枣树，另一棵也是枣树，哈哈哈。
![20261004_105843.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYUXzGWv9ugaGmfv1W9owNvuY9HmCkM83PY4RutS8yASU/20261004_105843.jpg)

我家门口有好多棵树，有杏树、枣树、枣树、榛子树
![20261004_105854.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaaUutver5VjXyjzFVRmmN9HfkwH6gmgy9HyL5tCUireN/20261004_105854.jpg)

不光门口，院子里还有好多枣树和其它果树，房子后边的花园里还有果树，不过我懒得去拍啦
![20261004_105914.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVi4Cyh1WhwX2wEcURmQ8VkcambNuqzLGwH9JBuS6rSJn/20261004_105914.jpg)

这棵枣树的果实巨大呀，非常好吃。
![20261004_110008.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmToJ9usVAVXdZHQRQV18bNNgSmGuVr9tu89r2icu2zdsk/20261004_110008.jpg)

原本我打算全家一起去饭店吃大餐，可是镇上没有太好的饭店
要带他们去牛庄吃馅饼，他们还都嫌远，怕下大暴雨，于是就在家凑合一顿吧
![20261004_163535.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdbAdMyfta4tBfDWjJHe4ZKHL6acngoXqH6pBBmXx4fb7/20261004_163535.jpg)

姐夫去西柳买了好多熟食
![20261004_163539.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPgQzvYRhbi3yWQqSwHgVmhYBBvusGNsVsSgJK25JZ8zU/20261004_163539.jpg)

还有花生米
![20261004_163542.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbVoYk53itjMntEvVX2QtD7fqbWuinthkrECt58TooV2T/20261004_163542.jpg)

猪肝和香肠
![20261004_163546.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRbZBp6vV77yBJENbcbeVwu4hj1NSfCXzFbGGtmrdQb2w/20261004_163546.jpg)

鸡胗和酱牛肉啥的一大堆
![20261004_163549(0).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfVm39cyBZczbA5BANspPPcz4x64sERakLTpHKZKjXSCo/20261004_163549(0).jpg)

还有大虾
![20261004_163553.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQbqz8kvdH9bNa8j7iZhAdVL6ZiAikmzi7u2JwsNV5qrD/20261004_163553.jpg)

辣椒炒肚
![20261004_163556.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWmRxgLHTic65dEZNbPWsPHY7dAuBBYP5T2PQifbww7oS/20261004_163556.jpg)

还有螃蟹
![20261004_163558.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTPbdQF6pDdbRKPwSgh4KK6FVZpmf5KPnzPZ5sziBDcx6/20261004_163558.jpg)

还有饺子
![20261004_163606.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVzFuMyu3Ss7CVd5CPrMPHyJHMEKTg8Jdy32DjSfzq3LS/20261004_163606.jpg)

饭菜可能没饭店的丰盛，但是全家一起吃还是其乐融融，就是那个螃蟹父亲花大价钱买的，结果螃蟹很小，又被熟人骗了，哎。

对了，我们还给母亲订了个好利来的小蛋糕，一路车程颠簸，形象有些受影响，但是吃起来还是非常美味的，用另外一个手机拍的照，就不来回倒照片过来啦。

饭后六点多，外边下着小雨，我们冒雨开高速去媳妇妈妈家，高速黑漆漆的一片，雨水以及地面反光极度影响视线，到媳妇家雨还变大了，找车位也废了好大劲。不过这都不算啥，我们上楼时竟然被困电梯里，还好最终有惊无险地逃了出来。

所以这真是丰富多彩的一天啊，哈哈哈。

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deanliu/2423uysaJaxUBQg3JNpCbBn1W7xud4ySniuziWJ6WYSwTkXs5SfoKXzpdaQEeN6ZvMntc.png)
HELLO HIVERS !! 🌍👋
今天想分享一個想法，是從一則看似跟去中心化有關的新聞所啟發的，期待可以引發更多關於我們這個全球社區怎麼持續發展的好想法。 Today I want to share an idea sparked by a news story that, at first glance, looks like a win for decentralization. I'm hoping it gets us talking about how this global community of ours can keep growing.
我們先來講講一個上個月在美國加州的有趣新聞。2026 年 9 月 9 日傍晚，加州熱浪，熱到誇張。全州電力需求全開，偏偏，太陽一下山，白天最會發電的太陽能板就準時下班。用電高峰才剛開始，供電主力卻走到尾聲，電網供需產生嚴重不匹配的大問題。照以往的劇本，電力公司只能二選一：點燃平常閒置、又貴又髒的天然氣尖峰電廠，或是準備分區停電，讓大家一起體驗汗流浹背的人生。 So here's a fun story from California last month. On the evening of September 9, 2026, a heat wave hit, and it was brutal. Power demand across the state went through the roof. And of course, right as the sun went down, the solar panels that carry the grid all day clocked out right on schedule. The evening peak was just getting started, but the main power source was already heading home. Supply and demand were badly out of sync. In the old playbook, the utility had two choices: fire up the expensive, dirty gas peaker plants that sit idle most of the year, or start rolling blackouts and let everyone enjoy a nice sweaty evening together.
但是，那天晚上出現了第三個選項。散在加州各地住家裡、超過 14 萬顆家用儲能電池，在三個小時內一起把電送回電網，高峰超過 580 MW。其中大約 11 萬顆是特斯拉的 Powerwall，貢獻 517 MW，其他品牌的電池則補上剩下的 63 MW。 But that night, a third option showed up. More than 140,000 home batteries scattered across California pushed power back into the grid together for three hours, peaking at over 580 MW. About 110,000 of them were Tesla Powerwalls, contributing 517 MW, and batteries from other brands covered the remaining 63 MW.
（英文報導：Solar Builder、mgrid） (Coverage: Solar Builder, mgrid)
580 MW 是什麼概念？一座典型的天然氣尖峰電廠大約 50 到 250 MW。也就是說，一堆平常默默待在車庫角落、沒人多看一眼的電池，合體之後變成好幾座電廠。這種玩法叫「虛擬電廠」VPP。 So how big is 580 MW? A typical gas peaker plant runs somewhere between 50 and 250 MW. In other words, a bunch of batteries quietly sitting in garages, the kind nobody looks at twice, teamed up and turned into several power plants. This setup is called a "virtual power plant," or VPP.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deanliu/23uQn7dBfQ77agcQvuXY1vvLhqs18bvvDQmjGQKMrhgwB3Tr9xHUNRsoz6DDjWpBxSbHc.png)
## 那這些電池主人打什麼算盤？ ／ So What's in It for the Battery Owners?
答案其實很簡單：利之所趨。 The answer is quite simple: money works.
這些電池平常照顧自家用電，只有在電網真的撐不住時才被叫出來支援，主人因此拿到補償。電網也很樂意付這筆錢，因為比起花好幾年、好幾億美元蓋一座一年只用幾十個小時的電廠，跟大家「借電」便宜太多了。有興趣的朋友請自己去研究一下這個新聞或這個商業機制。 Most of the time these batteries only satisfy their own needs. Only when the grid is really struggling do they get called in to help, and the owners get paid for it. The grid is happy to pay, too. Compared to spending years and hundreds of millions of dollars on a plant that only runs a few dozen hours a year, "borrowing" power from people's homes is way cheaper. If you're curious, go dig into the story or how this VPP business model works.
我讀到這則新聞時，第一個反應是「去中心化萬歲」😂，但仔細一想好像是太誇大了。第二個反應冷靜一點：這件事其實沒那麼去中心化。580 MW 裡有 517 MW 是透過特斯拉一家公司的平台調度，不少電池也不是住戶自己的，而是由太陽能公司 Sunrun 擁有或營運，什麼時候放電的規則則是州政府定的。節點很分散，指揮權很集中。 My first reaction when I read this was "Long live decentralization!"😂 But on second thought, that felt like a stretch. My second, calmer reaction: this isn't actually that decentralized. Of the 580 MW, 517 MW was dispatched through one company's platform, Tesla's. Plenty of the batteries aren't even owned by the homeowners; they're owned or operated by the solar company Sunrun. And the rules for when to discharge are set by the state. The nodes are spread out, but the command is very centralized.
但這不影響它精彩的地方。這件事真正打動我的是：分散的力量要動得起來，靠的是兩件事：平常就待在那裡，以及需要的時候有人願意付錢。 That doesn't take away from what makes it exciting, though. What really struck me is this: for scattered power to actually move, it takes two things: being there all along, and someone willing to pay when it's needed.
## Hive 又不儲能，我們能做什麼？ ／ Hive Doesn't Store Energy, So What Can We Do?
對，Hive 沒有電池，也沒有車庫。它是一條純虛擬的鏈，看起來很難有「今晚缺電」這種實體的緊急需求。 True, Hive has no batteries and no garages. It's a purely virtual chain, and it's hard to picture it facing a physical emergency like "we're short on power tonight."
但我想了一陣子，發現 Hive 其實有自己版本的「家用電池」。如果用一句話來形容 Hive 可能可以發揮的獨特之處，或許可以這樣總結： But after chewing on it for a while, I realized Hive actually has its own version of "home batteries." If I had to sum up in one sentence what Hive could uniquely bring to the table, it might go like this:
很多分散在各地的人，在同一個時間點，各做一件小事，立刻拿到錢，並留下誰都改不了的紀錄。
Lots of real people spread across the world, at the same moment, each doing one small thing, getting paid instantly, and leaving a record no one can change.
拆開來看： Let's break it down:
分散在各地的人：從拉丁美洲到非洲，Hive 上有不少人位在國際企業最難觸及的地方。 People spread across the world: From Latin America to Africa, plenty of folks on Hive live in places international companies have the hardest time reaching.
同一個時間點：跨時區，代表永遠有人醒著。 At the same moment: Different time zones mean someone is always awake.
可即刻動員的能量：拍張照、回答幾個問題、去外面不遠的地方，在指示下確認一些事等等，門檻不用高，存在跟可信是重點。 Ready-to-go capacity: Snap a photo, answer a few questions, pop out somewhere nearby and check something by following instructions. The bar doesn't need to be high. Being there and being trustworthy is what counts.
立刻拿到錢：這是 Hive 最被低估的超能力。3 秒出一個區塊，轉帳不收手續費。在別的地方付十塊錢報酬，手續費可能比報酬還貴；在 Hive，幾乎一塊錢就是一塊錢。 Getting paid instantly: This is Hive's most underrated superpower. A new block every 3 seconds, and no transfer fees. Elsewhere, sending someone a tiny reward can cost more in fees than the reward itself. On Hive, a dollar is pretty much a dollar.
改不了的紀錄：誰在什麼時間交了什麼，寫上鏈就是寫上鏈，事後吵架有憑有據。 A record no one can change: Who turned in what, and when. Once it's on chain, it's on chain. If there's an argument later, the receipts are right there.
## 一支「待命模式」的全球團隊 ／ A Global Team on Standby Mode
把這五件事放在一起，我腦中浮現的畫面是：一支全球團隊，所有人平常都處於待命模式。 Put these five things together, and the picture in my head is: a global team where everyone is on standby by default.
平常大家照樣過日子、發文、按讚。沒有人領月薪，沒有辦公室，沒有固定成本。有案子進來，任務就被切成小塊，丟給剛好在對的地方、對的時間的人。做完，錢立刻進錢包，紀錄留在鏈上。案子結束，大家回到待命，繼續過自己的日子。當然，得有人出面組織，組織管理這種事情，很難去中心化的。 Day to day, everyone just lives their life, posts, upvotes. Nobody's on a salary, there's no office, no fixed costs. When a job comes in, it gets chopped into small tasks and handed to whoever happens to be in the right place at the right time. Task done, money lands in the wallet instantly, record stays on chain. When the job wraps up, everyone goes back on standby and carries on. Of course, someone has to step up and organize. Organizing and managing things is pretty hard to decentralize.
這是不是跟那 14 萬顆電池很像？平常待在車庫，需要時一起出力，出完力領錢，然後回去繼續發文章。 Sound a lot like those 140,000 batteries? Sitting in the garage most of the time, pitching in when needed, getting paid, then going back to writing posts.
傳統公司要在 30 個國家同時做一件事，得先在 30 個國家找人、簽約、開帳戶、處理跨國匯款，光行政就夠人打退堂鼓了。但這支想像中的待命隊伍則是早就在那裡了，只差一個發號施令的案子。 A traditional company that wants to do something in 30 countries at once has to find people, sign contracts, open accounts, and sort out cross-border payments in all 30. The paperwork alone is enough to make anyone give up. But this imaginary standby crew is already out there. All it's missing is a job to get things rolling.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deanliu/23uQn7dBfQ77agcQvuXY1vvLhqs18bvvDQmjGQKMrhgwB3Tr9xHUNRsoz6DDjWpBxSbHc.png)
## 舉個例子：新口味飲料全球上架情況如何？ ／ Example: How's That New Drink Doing on Shelves Worldwide?
假設一家消費品牌要在 20 個國家同時推出新口味飲料。上市那天，品牌最想知道的是：貨真的上架了嗎？價格標對了沒？促銷海報有沒有貼，消費者第一反應如何？ Say a consumer brand launches a new drink flavor in 20 countries at the same time. On launch day, here's what the brand wants to know most: Did the product actually hit the shelves? Is the price tag right? Is the promo poster up? What do people think at first sip?
在大城市的連鎖超市，這些可以派人去查。但在奈及利亞路邊的小雜貨店、菲律賓巷口的小店，品牌幾乎無從得知。就算找到在地人幫忙看，要付他一筆小錢也麻煩得要命。 At big-city supermarket chains, you can send someone to check. But at a roadside shop in Nigeria or a little corner store down an alley in the Philippines, the brand has basically no idea. Even if they find a local to take a look, paying that person a small amount is a total pain.
這正是待命隊伍的主場。上市當天，品牌發出任務：「請到附近的店拍下貨架，回報價格。」各地的 Hive 用戶出門買菜順手拍一張，甚至可以喝一罐試喝給意見，當下領到報酬，照片和時間戳留在鏈上。日後品牌和通路吵「到底有沒有上架」，翻紀錄就好。 This is exactly where the standby crew shines. On launch day, the brand sends out a task: "Go to a store near you, snap a photo of the shelf, and report the price." Hive users everywhere grab a shot while doing their grocery run, maybe even try a can and share their thoughts, get paid on the spot, and the photo and timestamp stay on chain. If the brand and the retailer later fight over whether the product was really on the shelf, just check the record.
再延伸一步，也可以是在地意見：「這個口味在你們那邊會受歡迎嗎？」「這個包裝在你們文化裡有沒有奇怪的含意？」全球品牌最怕在某個市場鬧笑話，而這支隊伍剛好散布在各種文化裡。 Take it one step further and it could be local opinions: "Would this flavor go down well where you live?" "Does this packaging mean something weird in your culture?" Global brands dread embarrassing themselves in some market, and this crew just happens to be spread across all kinds of cultures.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/deanliu/23tvW8Z4xgPvjRYrp7rGrnPbLgyurr4AKTba5hCvWVnYm32TPZK28TFD3cixESTr2P15r.png)
## 這支隊伍要怎麼建起來？ ／ How Do We Build This Crew?
理想很豐滿，現實很骨感，總是得有人捲起袖子來嘗試看看。以下是我跟 AI 一起想的幾個建議，刺激一下大家想法： Sounds great on paper, but reality is never that neat. Someone has to roll up their sleeves and give it a shot. Here are a few suggestions I brainstormed with AI, just to get the ideas flowing:
一、從現有社群出發。 Hive 上本來就有很多依語言、地區分的社群，它們就是現成的各地小隊。不必從零招募，只要問一句：「有誰願意登記待命？」 1. Start with existing communities. Hive already has plenty of communities organized by language and region. They're ready-made local squads. No need to recruit from scratch. Just ask: "Who's up for joining the standby list?"
二、建立待命名冊，但只登記到城市。 每個人自願填寫所在城市、會的語言、能做的任務類型、方便的時段。注意，只到城市就好，不要精確地址。我們要建的是待命隊伍，不是監控網。 2. Build a standby roster, but only down to the city. Everyone voluntarily fills in their city, languages, the kinds of tasks they can handle, and when they're free. City only, no exact addresses. We're building a standby crew, not a surveillance network.
三、先辦演習，再接真案。 就像消防隊不會等火災才第一次拉水管。可以先辦社群內部的練習任務，例如「全球同一天拍下一顆雞蛋的價格」，順便做出一張全世界的雞蛋物價地圖。好玩、有話題，也讓大家熟悉流程。 3. Run drills before taking real jobs. Firefighters don't wait for a fire to roll out the hose for the first time. Start with practice tasks inside the community, like "everyone around the world photographs the price of an egg on the same day," and build a global egg price map while you're at it. It's fun, it gets people talking, and everyone learns the ropes.
四、把任務做成標準格式。 照片怎麼拍、問卷怎麼填，都要有統一規格，不然收回來 20 個國家的資料，20 種格式，整理的人會哭。 4. Standardize the tasks. How to take the photo, how to fill out the survey, it all needs a common format. Otherwise you get data from 20 countries in 20 different formats, and whoever has to clean it up will cry.
五、第一個客戶不用找大企業。 先從小品牌、獨立遊戲團隊、需要跨國資料的研究者開始。案子小沒關係，重點是累積成功案例，讓人看到這支隊伍真的動得起來。 5. The first client doesn't have to be a big company. Start with small brands, indie game studios, researchers who need data from different countries. Small jobs are fine. What matters is racking up success stories so people can see this crew really works.
六、新手從簡單任務開始。 拍照、回報價格這類容易驗證的任務先做，累積紀錄後再接需要判斷力的在地意見調查。 6. Newcomers start with simple tasks. Photos and price reports first, things that are easy to verify. Build a track record, then move up to local opinion surveys that need more judgment.
## 避不開的一題：怎麼讓人信得過？ ／ The Question We Can't Dodge: How Do We Make It Trustworthy?
當然，有錢可拿的地方就有人想亂來，隨便拍一張網路圖、亂填一份問卷來領錢。這在 Hive 不是新聞，自動投票和刷量的故事大家都聽過。 Of course, wherever there's money, someone will try to game it: grab a random photo off the internet, fill out a survey with junk, and collect the reward. That's not news on Hive. We've all heard the stories about autovoting and farming.
所以這支隊伍能不能成立，關鍵不在找不找得到人，而在能不能設計出一套讓人信得過的機制。付錢的客戶最在意的就是這個：資料是真的嗎？人是真的嗎？ So whether this crew can work doesn't come down to finding people. It comes down to whether we can design a system people can trust. That's what paying clients care about most: Is the data real? Are the people real?
可以想的方向很多：同一任務派給多人交叉比對；照片要求現場即時拍攝；做得好的人累積可信度、接到更好的案子；隨機抽查；甚至要求接案者先押一點東西當保證。每個方法各有漏洞，怎麼組合才擋得住有心人，這題都可以持續探索，還沒有好的答案，大家一起想想。有沒有覺得這個如果做起來，真的很"Hive"？ There are lots of directions to explore: send the same task to several people and cross-check; require photos taken live on the spot; let people who do good work build up credibility and land better jobs; random spot checks; maybe even ask workers to put something down as a deposit. Every method has holes. How to combine them to keep the bad actors out is something we can keep working on. There's no great answer yet, so let's figure it out together. Don't you think that if this actually took off, it would be very "Hive"?
## 希望有人能想想，能去做 ／ Hoping *Someone* Picks This Up and Runs With It
電網缺電時，有人想到了車庫裡的電池。那麼世界上還有哪些「需要很多人、在很多地方、同時做一點小事」的需求，正在等這支待命隊伍？ When the grid ran short, someone thought of the batteries in the garage. So what other needs out there, the kind that take "lots of people, in lots of places, each doing a little something at the same time," are waiting for this standby crew?

It’s no more than 200 metres long, but along that stretch it brings together many of the city’s wonders and plenty of places to visit, not least because this street is crossed by other, even smaller streets that hold their own treasures, or because Calle Císter itself is lined with the city’s iconic buildings. But before I tell you about my walk and everything there is to see here, I’ll explain why I consider it historic and important. When I first arrived here, the first place I rented was a small studio flat 12 km from the city. But when my family joined me, we needed somewhere bigger, and finding a flat to rent was quite an ordeal, particularly given the conditions required. We couldn’t be too fussy or make too many demands, and we managed to find a flat thanks to a sort of estate agency located on this street. I went to one of those buildings to sign the contract and meet the flat’s owners. That moment was special and I’ll never forget it. As the title suggests, this trip out west takes us to the fourth to last state that I will be covering with these posts.  All we have left after this is West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.  It's been a heck of a ride hasn't it?  

Part of me feels like it was just yesterday that we were visiting Alabama.  Honestly, I almost wish we were visiting Alabama.  I think it was easier to find three songs for that state than it has been for Washington.  

<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23z74tBCz2CPjv1QCEZzP11StpfamoBbxevsDJYW9v3BzgWBuxfZmc9A42GwwH65AmmuA.png)</center>

--------------------------


The real problem with Washington is the fact that there are tons of songs about Washington DC, or George Washington, or Washingtons (in relation to currency), but there just aren't a lot of songs that I can say with 100% certainty that they are about Washington state on the west coast of the US.  

Which means I had to do a bit more digging than I normally do for this post.  I did end up finding three songs to share with you, and I am fairly certain they are all pointing in the right direction when they mention Washington, but you will just have to listen for yourself and see.

I actually expected Washington to be easier than this... Shows what I know!

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/od9UsmfIUK0?si=-30fx1UlNRE5doP7" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

-------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=od9UsmfIUK0&list=RDod9UsmfIUK0&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

I used to be a pretty big Zach Bryan fan, then he let the fame get to him a little too much and he said and did some things he probably shouldn't have.  That doesn't mean I am going to stop listening to his music, but I don't find myself listening to him as much as I used to.  "Washington Lilacs" is the song I am picking from him.  After doing a bit of Google searching, I did verify that Washington state is known for its lilacs, so I am about 99.9% certain this song is definitely about the correct Washington.  

Despite his ill advised choices, Bryan does have a good way of putting a song together and he delivers them in a way that is very moody and introspective.  He reminds me of a bit more mellow Jason Isbell.  I got the chance to see Bryan several years ago when he wasn't quite as popular as he is now.  Instead of headlining a show, he was the third or fourth opening act before the big players got on stage.  Despite that, he did a fantastic job and though I only knew one of his songs at the time, he totally blew me away.

Despite how things have turned out, I am still glad I got to see him live before the fame and fortune caught up with him.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/AVp9FPtwZOQ?si=SQGSPO3Q_ggMGK-v" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

---------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AVp9FPtwZOQ&list=RDAVp9FPtwZOQ&start_radio=1)

---------------------------

Long before he became a household name with his gravel voice and a karaoke favorite with "The Gambler", Kenny Rogers was part of a band called The First Edition.  During that time he had this song called "My Washington Woman".  I can't say as though I have ever heard this song before today, but the funny thing is, the voice doesn't even sound like him.  If you played this for me and asked me to tell you who was singing, Kenny Rogers is probably the last person I would have guessed.

Yet, it is him, and "My Washington Woman" does have a reference to Washington in it.  In fact, I think it also references Seattle which was the clincher for me to include it.  With that piece of geography in place, there is little chance people might think he is talking about DC, or the person.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/QufbRiVrBJw?si=PZLN7ph1mt3amKnN" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

------------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QufbRiVrBJw&list=RDQufbRiVrBJw&start_radio=1)

-------------------------------

For the last song, I am actually going to share two.  I know, I know, I said it was hard enough to find three, but leave it to good old Bob Dylan to give us plenty of songs about the great Pacific Northwest.  The first one is "The Grand Coulee Dam", and this is a live version that I found on YouTube.  It takes a bit to get the the actual reference, but it is there towards the end.  You just have to listen pretty closely.  Especially since it is Dylan and a lot of people have trouble understanding him anyway!

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/8zWNJV2P_ZI?si=GKKB1eCW-6Pw749D" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

----------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8zWNJV2P_ZI&list=RD8zWNJV2P_ZI&start_radio=1)

----------------------------

The original author of "Roving Gambler" is actually unknown, but Bob had a tendency to cover it from time to time.  You can actually find a bunch of different versions of it online both by him and by dozens of other artists that have covered it over the years.  There is a reference to Washington earlier in the song where he says he gambled up in Washington.  Since he also talks about "Frisco", I can only guess that he is talking about Washington state when he says "up north".  

So there you go.  We are getting close to the end now, and I am not sure what I am going to do from here on Tuesdays.  Maybe I will have to start using Scrobble or something.  We will see!

result.body: 我之前一直想过一个问题：为什么有些人上了年纪之后，会变得越来越自私？这几天，我似乎有点想明白了。 人之所以会受伤，大多是因为其中有感情。如果一个人对一切都变得自私一些，不再轻易投入自己的感情，那么确实可以大大减少自己受到的伤害，至少在情感上，不会那么容易被人左右和刺痛。 还有一个原因。人之所以会变得冷漠、自私，甚至被人称为“没感情”，很多时候其实是一种自我保护。 典型的例子就是古代帝王。他们所处的环境，本身就充满了利益和算计，身边的人也未必是真心相待。在这样的环境里，把自己的感情，或者说自己的弱点，隐藏起来，不轻易示于人前，也许反而是一种生存之道。 太重感情，有时候确实是一个人的弱点。 如果遇到同样重感情的人，两个人很容易惺惺相惜，成为知己。但现实往往是，人会因为利益而选择放弃感情，而这恰恰是最容易让重感情的人受伤的地方。 所以，人活到一定年纪，或许都会慢慢学会收回一些感情，不再轻易付出，也不再轻易相信。 从这个角度来说，所谓的“自私”和“无情”，未必真的意味着一个人变坏了。有时候，只不过是经历了一些事情之后，终于明白了保护自己。 太重感情，容易受伤；太相信别人，容易失望；太在意别人，容易失去自己。 所以，有时候我会觉得，人至无情，则无敌。 但反过来说，感情恰恰也是人区别于动物的重要标志之一。 人之所以伟大，之所以能够一代又一代地繁衍生息，之所以会被人爱、被人记住，其中一个很重要的原因，就是人是有感情的。 正因为有了感情，人与人之间才不会那么冷漠；正因为有了亲情、友情和爱情，我们的人生才有了温度，那些人与人之间的牵挂、陪伴和回忆，才会变得如此珍贵，也如此令人愉悦和怀念。 所以，感情既是一个人的软肋，也可能恰恰是一个人最珍贵的东西。 感情是脆弱的，因为它很容易让人受伤；感情又是伟大的，因为正是有了爱，人才能变得伟大。 ![yaomuyu-nepal-10489603_1920.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRmWFvJwynRDjRrEwtQPeexNp3pNKE9Wy1sMwxFB5CgGx/yaomuyu-nepal-10489603_1920.jpg) Image by Yao Muyu from Pixabay 佛教里讲因果。大意是说，每个人和每件事都有自己的因和果，今天发生的一切，都有它发生的原因。因此，不要轻易介入别人的因果。 以前，我对这些话一直很不理解，甚至觉得有些莫名其妙，多少带着一点迷信，似乎也没什么道理。 但人到中年以后，经历的事情多了，才慢慢明白，有些道理并不是一开始就能看懂的。 所谓“不要轻易介入别人的因果”，其实是有一定道理的。每个人都有自己的选择，也有自己需要承担的后果。很多事情看似与自己无关，却往往有着复杂的前因后果。如果轻易地介入别人的事情，甚至试图替别人解决问题，最后很可能不仅没有帮上忙，反而把自己卷进去，给自己惹来不必要的麻烦。 所以，用老百姓最通俗的一句话来总结就是： 不要多管闲事。

And I'm talking about myself, obviously, because I have many photographer friends who love those saturated and somewhat garish greens of our rainy season. But not me. I have to be honest and say that when I start looking at so much green, I tend to miss the "ochres and browns" of the dry season. And so, it's on days like these, wandering through the surrounding rural areas, that I end up "imagining" things differently, in different colors, a bit like "fabulating" everything and trying to adapt it to my preferences. One bee sting sends me to hospital, and I will be no more if one hundred have to sting me, and it nearly happened here. In my eagerness to get the bees on video, I wandered a bit too close, and suddenly a tribe of soldier bees flew all around my head. The zooming sounds of their flight were terrifying to hear, and I really thought that the bees would start to attack me. I also know that if one starts to slap the bees away, it will only make them angrier and more determined to attack.

So, come and see what happened, and the first 3 photos will show you the hive's layout. Then you will see the video and one final shot before I cleared out of there.
![059.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EpxsDdnVwCcMxsr2Naye1GEJwh19KZu6xbcEXjtQvCTxaEh57PueQ9DnMNL1y1RjG1C.JPG)

![070.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23wX1BfsnhvZ9cmUf6ER2KSKU1h8JAxFNUfAbVwAyZmTFGEHFC9wMF8Xnz9jcr63EKZ1L.JPG)

An unedited video, and you will see the shaky parts when the soldier bees decided to come out and warn me. 

https://youtu.be/QlJJYwANPUw

I don't know what kind of a tree this is, but I presume that there has to be some sweet tree sap that drew the bees, as it is an old tree with a scar where a branch that had been severed from the trunk.
![058.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EpxtG3XS13fbkdPsbKhX7DubRhKgpjmj5dcLdSsywtGGzMAawELYGZsRtx2nf5sc2cA.JPG)

So, it was a dangerous situation, and it just goes to show that one should also take care in nature. I slipped up this time in my eagerness to get the bees on video, but thankfully I knew not to panic, and that all I had to do was to slowly back away. This is not a first time for me to take shots of a bee swarm, but in the past, I never took videos of it and this time I decided that I just had to take a video, shaky or not. Will I go back there to get another video? Not on your life, as one video is enough Lol. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

Photos and words by Zac Smith. No AI and no Photoshop. All-Rights-Reserved.

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera. 

Until next time, shalom!

Sunday was a special day for me for a couple of reasons. Once, because we got to celebrate the birthday of a relative of mine at a nice place and secondly, because finally I had the chance to get closer to a horse and have some fun photographing animals in the stable. ![Having Fun At The Stable.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/48TKbKbPmkGcjEfoqhEA5yjquzJMBr8UrtZ1VexsBTsaZQ53oJdhbFqjmbj5xGdyt7.png) It's not the first time I got to pet a horse, but the previous occasions were really brief, as long as an animal is willing to stay in front of the visitors, while an iron fence is separating them from horse. I grew up in the city and even though I got to visit my grandparents in their village during summer breaks, there were no horses around. So you will understand why I was so happy on Sunday. The place we visited is a complex one, it is outside and far away from any city. It's a big property offering accommodation, riding lessons, organizing events and they have a nice restaurant with two or more terraces as well, for those looking to escape the city. They have a stable and a small animal park for smaller animals you can visit for free, if you served a meal in the restaurant and for a small fee, if you're just visiting. ![20261004_153127a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/Eoc7aDZf9nBchHuGFhFymQZJvfdtst8CwcgeMHcZDeN91Ehdv3DZsJPn8SGy5HQ15LL.JPG) At the time of our visit, there was one horse outside in the ring, one kid was riding it, or better said the instructor was leading the horse as this was just a normal walk. ![20261004_153129a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/Eokd4T4RC9dRgqGot6465zmpftrcKvpRhqfhrTavBD62bwYzLxdKoLEtDuHBbSYWm7N.JPG) If you look closer, you can see the circle marked on the ground and the horse knows to walk that circle, so I don't think there are problems there. ![20261004_153135a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/EoAbBQQoe2b1rmWsLEwmoWB3SUPzgHg22SuyZqCsDZBE3FzW2aSptp7hY3pkCnkmGvg.JPG) Although I've never had the chance to ride a horse, I think it's a great and fun experience for kids of his age. ![20261004_153340a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23x171hZuMYs8vStK1vVi2XT91sKXcdwWLiVnwF43duDC7HWQtUesQWdkXUzutPnhdEr7.JPG) For me, this is where the fun started in every sense of the word. We entered the stable and saw the horses. At that point I had two goals, not exactly compatible with each other, so I had to work magic to make it work. ![20261004_153346a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23wMaSoC7xQpUyHiUQ3ZGaNRKshbpxvCLnbaMxD4kSsDDMCoDaLVjwLp5j1uhzwaNjiXa.JPG) Moat of the horses were either tired, sleepy or bored, and only a handful of them showed interest in making friends with the visitors. ![20261004_153356a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xp4Y9rtHEQjNUaJJUAqfboMSPao4EWfeT3c64RH5P9QGymKyXgPWGB3nAezMSwrTUdZ.JPG) This white beauty was drinking water on its own, most likely hydration is automated to some degree. ![20261004_153441a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23wqhzd7D1MPXP4tTMfUvatA1EtjMvHDA4rNsnNhiU2vk8pkT4r1PnhtvDUShPsCwZNGW.jpg) As I mentioned above, I had two goals. One was to take, or try to take some decent photos and the other was to pet the horses, try to make friends with them. ![20261004_153444a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xySdGF83hizmvx98uoX7LQrVicbEz6fKyUfAnReYXj9BRYkXErYKzFkXRCwpm7Rbd5o.jpg) The second goal was easier to achieve, but the first one ... that was a headache. ![20261004_153500a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xKtdQhgVBNzvy4JYBrx6HnqcQmtyEGy89Gccjn5tpmmyN6WugD9T44Eswm4Fxws5zEn.JPG) When you have a moving animal of such size and an iron gate with bars so close to each other, you need a lot of luck and a lot of shots to get the job done. ![20261004_153522a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xowok861X2S8kDUjoHPDbXMM8Zg6SZqaRdieX7SWzVfYxury127nk1GBR4xLKu9Y6oy.JPG) ![20261004_153655a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23wgDc9W5X9ZWB87THxVukMeE5iKM8bwv2eWmGBfUbVzXiFwKMrQSWe29Kyn8hDyeHj3B.JPG) Unfortunately, these beauties were not interested in making friends with me, or anyone else. ![20261004_153733a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23tmFzcymgKfZMczdwgHEzzsSyDpYYZ4rNTzfJx5H8LjazmA8wQVW2Whf9iLM8tyzzENQ.JPG) ... aaaand this was my moment! Finally! These horses were not behind bars, they could stick their heads out freely and let visitors pet them and this beauty made the most of our love. ![20261004_153735a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23u63KtGY1TVDEUJMoCD22DZT1TQ8XAaTcXdXMhyiuqK9a9hmysXtfxL9pxYMo8KuuaPv.JPG) While the guy was petting him/her, I tried to take some photos, and this is what I ended up with. ![20261004_153736a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23uFPdPb7Rtpx3SNnWbpsAf3cAZKDbawv6Bm7vB49derHfi64oj1N5KxUwF7XDWXnN3zT.JPG) It was my second photo shoot with horses and I knew if I'm patient and take a bunch of photos, I can get some really funny ones at some point. ![20261004_153739(0)a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23tbsBFawrhjgYwDf4jfNuK6V8qq7fNXPx73QJto3MKBt2z6y9SHm8R2P8e4c3beoTfnT.JPG) After leaving I was thinking how lucky I am to have had this chance to connect with this lovely horse. He was really friendly and enjoyed being petted. Truth to be told, I was afraid to put my hand inside the bars at the previous places as I didn't know how the horses will react. One wrong move and they could break my arm, so I decided to play it safe and spend more time with this one. ![20261004_153809a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23u5zYyqYyHpdAGRxQTLSWunAr2W53CQCgJRKxUDwnSHUSwzKKbVvqzm51AFRFEWLg8Gm.JPG) ![20261004_153811a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23u62xA8CDNBKGXxb3rNF4ZY43MGweNmwwa7CXX4daHyeRXCcA3o1rTvXDCjRUjZuzTQs.JPG) It was really amazing how much love and kindness this horse had for us and how patient he was. ![20261004_153845a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23uFRmrNHSVw7HeAYfjp5zMqgdDtVTEbWfkGBLQgDKkoCjvg78DZVMEmKXpn8dbW6QJ7X.JPG) What surprised me even more was that he didn't take his eyes off of me. I don't know why was that, maybe curiosity as he could figure out we love him, and had no intention to harm or disturb him. ![20261004_153917a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23vsLA1D5TLQhupdg2HM7HHW5mwhLtWyHxHqxAcNYAWBh3SyxLyrECtsowsGgdt1haGkY.JPG) Look at this face. How can you not love it? ![20261004_153918a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23w2h7Xaw98HB5ejKEFr9UMXuFpjNCaAw2dwJyo6mqfA7DPLsMzThDznWp8v8aXX72eb7.JPG) ![20261004_153919(0)a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23vhwVcdiFH2xpPRpuJ1jeJuog6y8tF8eRvx54m2341W8rkJxeezsCV222ic2XWsToPX5.JPG) ![20261004_154017a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23uFPL3mXfDLY1Lrsaj6QpADoPNBCxKRuYXPZMoeGtTYinii2jPW1EsUwShxkdXAY4iDm.JPG) And to finish this post on a funny note, we got what we deserved 😂 a tongue out at the end, which was really cute by the way and no way offensive. How can you get mad at such a cutie pie? Thinking back to our visit, I could play with this horse all day long and would never get tired of him (or her). I don't know how much they can feel about what humans feel for them, probably a lot but I'd pet him all day. Most likely I would never ride a horse, because I have too much respect and love for them, so letting them carry me is definitely out of the question. I hope you liked this horse photo shoot as much as I do. It wasn't easy, but totally worth it.

Saludos. Revisando las publicaciones ancladas en la página de Holos me encontré con [esta]( https://peakd.com/hive-131951/@emiliorios/soledad-persistente-o-elegida-un-mal-moderno-cambiar-el-paradigma-de-estar-solo-reflexiones-esen) del amigo @emiliorios. En ella se desarrollan una serie de aspectos relacionados con el tema de la soledad, un tópico que aparece con mucha frecuencia en la conversación cotidiana. Les comento… Hace cuarenta años cuando llegué a la comunidad donde vivo no era común ver personas que vivieran solas. La gran mayoría compartía su vida en grupos familiares, algunos más extendidos que otros, donde cada integrante tenía un espacio que le servía para tener una intimidad relativa. Una de las excepciones a esa norma era el señor Manuel, mi vecino. Manuel era emigrante, chileno, cuando llegó a Venezuela ya sus hijos eran grandes en total eran cuatro y solo dos vinieron con él, tenían sus familias aparte y vivían en otro sector de la ciudad, Manuel vivía con su esposa y los hijos lo visitaban muy pocas veces al año. Cuando yo lo conocí ya la esposa había muerto, Manuel vivía solo en una casa bastante amplia, era celoso de su intimidad. En el largo tiempo que compartimos como vecinos nunca me invitó a entrar a su casa, hablábamos casi todos los días a través de la cerca perimetral, los dos de pie. A veces la conversación se extendía y no dejaba de sorprenderme como un hombre mayor como él podía aguantar tanto tiempo parado. Con frecuencia yo lo invitaba a mi casa pero Manuel siempre tenía alguna excusa para declinar la invitación. Lo que si aceptaba era la comida y el café que le llevaba hasta el portón que daba a la calle. En nuestras conversaciones nunca se quejaba de su soledad, al parecer le iba bien con eso. Mientras hablábamos era de lo más normal, dependiendo del tema se podía reír o fruncía el ceño. No pudiera decir que por estar solo él era un hombre triste. Con el paso del tiempo se fue haciendo mucho más mayor, superaba ampliamente los ochenta años y comenzó a perder la autonomía, ya no salía a hacer las compras, esa parte se la resolvíamos entre todos los que le conocíamos. A mi esposa y a mí nos preocupaba que estuviera solo. Varias veces al día lo llamábamos para escucharlo y saber que todo iba bien.
![imagen2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQBGRLSsDK2nPyXD3UXkkmxmBMndcgd5cFXYmuRUrmuEp/imagen2.jpg)
Un día vi en su casa un hombre joven, un muchacho. Luego supe que era su nieto, había venido a buscarlo para llevarlo a una residencia de ancianos. Nos dejo los datos por si estábamos interesados. Cada vez que tenía la oportunidad pasaba a visitarlo, me sorprendía ver lo rápido que iba cambiando, se iba transformando en otro Manuel, taciturno y muy deteriorado, quizá estaba enfermo. En ese lugar duró menos de un año, su salud empeoró rápidamente y finalmente murió… Ahora por mi casa es muy común ver más gente sola, la emigración de los jóvenes se hace notar, muchos hijos y nietos se han ido a buscar mejores oportunidades y los mayores van quedando atrás. Tengo varios conocidos que se han quedado solos, incluso tienen dificultades para valerse por sí mismos. Siempre hay una mano generosa que trata de ayudarlos pero la comunidad sola no puede hacer todo lo que se necesita. Hace falta más… La sociedad moderna ha hecho posible que la soledad sea una opción de vida. Y aunque siempre necesitaremos a los demás para no perecer ahora las personas pueden aprender a vivir en soledad, una opción tan válida como cualquier otra. En esas circunstancias la soledad no tiene por qué ser una desgracia. El problema se presenta cuando la soledad no llega como una elección personal sino como una imposición producto de las circunstancias. En ese caso sí puede convertirse en una tragedia porque no es algo que se hubiese deseado. Es el caso de muchos de mis vecinos y amigos a los que les cuesta llevar la vida sin el contacto con sus seres queridos. El asunto se ha vuelto bastante complejo y hace falta dedicar tiempo a pensar cuáles serían las mejores opciones para hacer más llevadera esa soledad no deseada… Gracias por tu tiempo. Greetings. While reviewing the pinned posts on the Holos page, I came across [this one]( https://peakd.com/hive-131951/@emiliorios/soledad-persistente-o-elegida-un-mal-moderno-cambiar-el-paradigma-de-estar-solo-reflexiones-esen) by my friend @emiliorios. In it, he explores a series of aspects related to the theme of loneliness, a topic that comes up very frequently in everyday conversation. Let me tell you… Forty years ago, when I arrived in the community where I live, it wasn’t common to see people living alone. The vast majority shared their lives in family groups—some more extended than others—where each member had a space that allowed for relative privacy. One exception to that norm was Mr. Manuel, my neighbor. Manuel was an immigrant from Chile; by the time he arrived in Venezuela, his children were already grown. He had four in total, but only two came with him—they had their own families and lived in another part of the city. Manuel lived with his wife, and his children visited him only a few times a year. By the time I met him, his wife had already passed away. Manuel lived alone in a fairly spacious house and was very protective of his privacy. During the long time we spent as neighbors, he never invited me into his home; we spoke almost every day over the perimeter fence, both of us standing. Sometimes the conversation would go on for a while, and it never ceased to amaze me how an elderly man like him could stand for so long. I often invited him to my house, but Manuel always had some excuse to decline the invitation. What he did accept, however, was the food and coffee I brought him right up to the gate facing the street.
![imagen2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQBGRLSsDK2nPyXD3UXkkmxmBMndcgd5cFXYmuRUrmuEp/imagen2.jpg)
In our conversations, he never complained about his loneliness; apparently, he was fine with it. While we talked, he was perfectly normal—depending on the topic, he would laugh or frown. I couldn’t say that being alone made him a sad man. As time went on, he grew much older—he was well past eighty—and began to lose his independence; he no longer went out to do his shopping, so those of us who knew him took care of that for him. My wife and I were worried that he was alone. We called him several times a day just to hear his voice and make sure everything was all right. One day I saw a young man—a boy—at his house. Later I learned he was his grandson; he had come to pick him up and take him to a nursing home. He left us his contact information in case we were interested. Whenever I had the chance, I’d stop by to visit him. I was surprised to see how quickly he was changing—he was becoming a different Manuel, taciturn and in very poor health; perhaps he was ill. He stayed there for less than a year; his health deteriorated rapidly, and he eventually passed away… Nowadays, around my neighborhood, it’s very common to see more people living alone; the exodus of young people is evident. Many children and grandchildren have left in search of better opportunities, and the elderly are left behind. I have several acquaintances who are now living alone; some even have difficulty taking care of themselves. There’s always a generous hand reaching out to help them, but the community alone can’t do everything that’s needed. More is needed… Modern society has made it possible for loneliness to be a lifestyle choice. And although we will always need others to survive, people can now learn to live in solitude—a choice just as valid as any other. Under those circumstances, loneliness doesn’t have to be a misfortune. The problem arises when loneliness isn’t a personal choice but rather an imposition brought about by circumstances. In that case, it can indeed become a tragedy because it is not something that was desired. This is the case for many of my neighbors and friends who struggle to get by without contact with their loved ones. The issue has become quite complex, and we need to take the time to consider what the best options might be to make this unwanted loneliness more bearable… Thank you for your time.

# a few cool historic properties in Fairhaven MA Good morning, and have a great day Recently, I was in Fairhaven to catch the sunrise at Fort Phoenix, but after the sunrise, I decided to stop in Fairhaven and take a walk, as they have some cool historic buildings there, and today I will share a few photos I took that morning. Starting with the First Congregational Church located on Center Street and was built around 1844–1845. It features a distinct red brick Gothic Revival design with a prominent four-stage bell tower The congregation represents the oldest religious group in Fairhaven. It was originally established on July 23, 1794, at that time, New Bedford still included the lands of present-day Fairhaven and Acushnet. An interesting detail I just read about: Their original meeting house featured a bell purchased directly from the historic foundry of Paul Revere in 1796. That original bell hung in the old church cupola until 1914, when it was bought by the town selectmen to serve as a fire alarm for the Oxford School
![historic properties fairhaven.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/EnYNWeB3Broi88LLRJa6FR7SeHFxQbPd2D9iqzyno38GTrbJnYywcJgbcDCp7XifuRv.jpg) **Sony A7iv 17mm F11 1/2 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/EnYNWeB3Broi88LLRJa6FR7SeHFxQbPd2D9iqzyno38GTrbJnYywcJgbcDCp7XifuRv.jpg)**

And next up The Millicent Library, located in Fairhaven, Massachusetts, is a striking Richardsonian Romanesque masterpiece designed by architect Charles Brigham. Dedicated on January 30, 1893, the library was given to the town by the wealthy industrialist and Standard Oil tycoon Henry Huttleston Rogers as a memorial to his daughter, Millicent, who tragically passed away at age 17. The building features rugged granite block construction, terracotta accents, a prominent conical tower, and exceptional stained-glass windows—including one portraying Millicent herself as the Greek goddess of poetry
![historic properties fairhaven-2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/245Sc75edjZJLchNRsm4hSwLSHRMooKEdgfKVTb4EC2SCCNvie2meu6hdi2JmkFq1ef2C.jpg) **Sony A7iv 19mm F11 1/3 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/245Sc75edjZJLchNRsm4hSwLSHRMooKEdgfKVTb4EC2SCCNvie2meu6hdi2JmkFq1ef2C.jpg)**

And the town hall Standard Oil industrialist Henry Huttleston Rogers and his first wife, Abbie, gave the building as a gift to the town. It was designed by Charles Brigham , and it opened in 1892.Original It originally held town offices, a post office, and a police station complete with three iron-barred jail cells
![historic properties fairhaven-3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23rAZM2DmyGAU571onSrArRuYz6c3YPdHTXXrTvq4nuGDx4oxKNncBdLJvy3RtYpyshjd.jpg) **Sony A7iv 22mm F11 1/2 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23rAZM2DmyGAU571onSrArRuYz6c3YPdHTXXrTvq4nuGDx4oxKNncBdLJvy3RtYpyshjd.jpg)**

And lastly the Memorial Unitarian Church Erected around 1901 and was also a gift from industrialist Henry Huttleston Rogers in memory of his mother.

Saludos querida comunidad, aunque falta un poco más de dos meses para la navidad, es este precisamente el mejor momento para comenzar para los encargos navideños, así tanto los clientes como yo nos veremos apresurados, por eso decidí hacer una versión mini de los amigurumis del pesebre navideño, para poder ofrecerle a mis clientes más opciones, comenzando en esta oportunidad por la Virgen María con el niño Jesús en brazos, para después incluir a San José en este proyecto, esperando les guste 😊 > Greetings, dear community! Although Christmas is still a little over two months away, this is precisely the best time to start taking Christmas orders so that neither my clients nor I feel rushed. That is why I decided to create a mini version of the Nativity scene amigurumis to offer my clients more options; I am starting with the Virgin Mary holding Baby Jesus, and plan to include Saint Joseph in the project later on. I hope you like it! 😊
https://i.imgur.com/iJNYddI.png

Proceso / Process

Para este proyecto usé hilo acrílico para crochet y ganchillo de 1.25mm, comencé haciendo la suela de la sandalia con un ovalo de 12 puntadas, cambié a hilo color piel y trabajé dos hileras y luego una hilera con 4 disminuciones en la punta para continuar con 8 puntadas por 3 hileras, uní las piernas por 2 cadenas y continué por 4 hileras, aparte hice la falda de 20 puntadas en circulo por 9 hileras, uní al torso y continué por 3 hileras antes de unir los brazos, hice disminuciones hasta obtener el cuello. > For this project, I used acrylic crochet yarn and a 1.25mm hook; I started by making the sandal sole using an oval of 12 stitches, switched to skin-colored yarn and worked two rows, followed by a row with 4 decreases at the toe, then continued with 8 stitches for 3 rows; I joined the legs with 2 chains and worked for another 4 rows. Separately, I made the skirt—working in the round with 20 stitches for 9 rows—attached it to the torso, and worked 3 more rows before attaching the arms, then made decreases until the neck was formed.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/irenenavarroart/AJkTPrWahUgWtDfgMW27YjcELFonMg6jw9TnGbiHGVL1mgDCXPkJ18KhAJNneHi.jpg https://i.imgur.com/iJNYddI.png
Para el cuello cambié a color piel y para la cabeza hice 6 aumentos por hileras hasta obtener 36, coloqué los ojos e hice 6 disminuciones por hilera rellenando antes de cerrar, para el cabello hice un círculo de 24 puntadas y sobre este hice 6 mechones de cabello. > For the neck, I switched to a skin tone, and for the head, I worked 6 increases per round until reaching 36 stitches; I inserted the eyes and then worked 6 decreases per round, stuffing the piece before closing it. For the hair, I made a circle of 24 stitches and worked 6 strands of hair onto it.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/irenenavarroart/AJoKadQQNqinjVBSw5xAPP6919aV16RV1PtB8p7wTn1ZLYmngZkeCD5fKTeB465.jpg https://i.imgur.com/iJNYddI.png
Para el niño Jesús trabajé la cabeza con 8 puntos bajos en un anillo y 8 aumentos, 16 puntos bajos por cinco hileras, luego 8 disminuciones y cambié a hilo blanco para el cuerpo haciendo aumentos nuevamente para obtener 16, hice el borde antes de la hilera de disminuciones de cierre, el cabello lo hice igual que la cabeza pero con un borde de 3 cadenas y punto deslizados consecutivamente. Para el manto de la virgen hice 27 cadenas de base para trabajar en recto pero usando el último punto para hacer 3 aumentos por 6 hileras y lograr el ancho de la cabeza, trabaje por 10 hileras más e hice el borde con hilo color trigo. > For the Baby Jesus, I worked the head starting with 8 single crochet stitches in a magic ring, followed by 8 increases; I worked 16 single crochet stitches for five rows, then 8 decreases. I switched to white yarn for the body, increasing again to reach 16 stitches, and added a border before the final row of decreases used to close the piece. I made the hair the same way as the head but added a border of 3-chain segments followed by consecutive slip stitches. > > For the Virgin's mantle, I started with a foundation chain of 27 stitches to work back and forth; I worked 3 increases in the last stitch over 6 rows to match the width of the head, worked for another 10 rows, and finished the border using wheat-colored yarn.

Hello everyone, hello hive friends.. hope everyone's doing great today where ever part of the world you are right now..

The beauty of the colors during sunset reminds us that a beautiful day is coming tomorrow.
Last week, while we were on our way home and already riding the ferryboat that had just left the port, I was amazed by the beauty of the slowly setting sun. Although the sun was still quite high, the colors in the sky were already beautiful, and their golden rays were reflected across the sea.
I wanted to take some photos, but it was difficult for me because I was sitting too far from the window. There were four of us together, and my niece was sitting beside the window. He had joined us for a little trip and was only seven years old.
